failures.evidence: check-ci-filters.sh passes when a ci.yaml go command that the table claims gains a package outside its job's filter. ci_filter_coverage.py:405-417 accepts a step's go line when the Run's pinned text is a substring of it (`squash(r.text) in squash(line)`), and computes the closure only of the Run's own packages. Probe on a trial merge with main: ci.yaml:2246 changed to `go test -tags multiprocess -count=1 -timeout 20m -v ./cmd/broker ./internal/routing/`. The check exits 0 ('broker-multiprocess: 278 files, 0 uncovered'), but `go list -deps -test -tags multiprocess ./internal/routing/` compiles packages/envoy/internal/routing, and PathsFilter(broker_multiprocess).covers('packages/envoy/internal/routing/match.go') is False. broker-multiprocess would then test routing while a routing change skips it, on the pull request and on main. The same append to envoy-go-race's listener step also passed, as packages/envoy/** covers it there. Red test, commit 5b6fb964 on legion/INFRA-520: the case 'a package added to a go command the table claims, outside the job's filter' in .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh. The fixture's step runs `go test ./cmd/app ./lib ./other`, and the case expects exit 1 and output naming other. Command: `PATH=<python with PyYAML>:$PATH bash .github/scripts/check-ci-filters.test.sh` prints 'FAIL: fails', 'FAIL: names the package the job now also tests', 'Results: 36 passed, 2 failed'. Fix in the check: hold the whole go line to the Run (the packages after the flags equal r.pkgs), or compute the closure from the packages the line names.
